title: The outOfReach cache invalidation in recordInterest decides money, but every committed test passes without it. A payment dated after the netting PLB L6 and reconciled with it then costs the netting L6's other payment for good: 4.40 credited where 6.00 is.
evidence: outOfReachOf (remittances.ts:1068-1078) caches interestOutOfReach per take-back PLB L6 for the whole pass. recordInterest's `interest.outOfReach.delete(adjustment.id)` (:1236) is what makes it read again once that L6 writes. Mutant A deletes that line. interest.db.test.ts and ledger-oracle.db.test.ts still pass, 54 of 54. apps/worker is in no Stryker shard. I added a scratch probe: one-line-paid.835 reconciled, then one-line-netted.835 with a copy of one-line-rest-paid.835 re-dated 2026-09-01 (after the netting L6), all before one reconcile, then one more reconcile. At the head the result is 600 credited against 600 of cash, the same as uploading and reconciling in date order. Under mutant A the same order gives 440 against 600. L1 holds [100, -100, 440] and L2 holds nothing: the late payment was written on L1 from a stale cache after the netting L6 reached L1, so the take-back owes 4.40 it can never follow, and B's 6.00 waits for good. The in-order run still gives 600, so the property and the LED-24 tests cannot tell. Every order they generate dates the netting L6 last (interest.test.ts:1133-1141 'X (dated last)'; :1196-1200; the one-line '*.835' fixtures date one-line-rest-paid.835 before one-line-netted.835).
fix: Add a red database test: an LED-24 synth variant with a payment of the chain dated after the netting PLB L6, uploaded with it before one reconcile, with an expected.json row. Assert 6.00 in both that order and date order, and check that it fails with the delete removed. Extend the property at interest.test.ts:1118 to date a payment after X. It should also model the per-pass cache, or the worker's composition should be tested directly.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every claim reproduced on the branch head, which is now 98bb9c00 (the branch has moved past 9824f4e9). The cache line it names was added by this PR (git log -S finds it in 1fda5637, MONEY-R4-1), and claude/build-platform has no outOfReach code at all.

Mechanism: outOfReachOf (remittances.ts:1068-1078) caches interestOutOfReach for each take-back PLB L6 for the whole pass. When the netting L6 is processed, unplacedOf calls paidLinesOf for the later paying L6, which caches the netting L6's own entry before it has written anything, so the entry is empty. The delete at :1236 is what clears that entry once the netting L6 writes. interestOutOfReach reads only the L6's draws (fixed for the pass) and its own writes, so deleting on write is a complete invalidation, and the head code is correct.

Probe (scratch test in my clone; loadVariant changes 260701 to 260901 in one-line-rest-paid.835, so it is dated 2026-09-01, after the netting L6's 2026-08-03): reconcile one-line-paid.835, upload one-line-netted.835 and the re-dated copy, reconcile, reconcile again.
- Head: L1 [100, -100], L2 [600], 600 credited against 600 of cash.
- Mutant A (the delete line removed): L1 [100, -100, 440], L2 [], 440 against 600. The assertion fails exactly as the finding says.
- Uploading the re-dated payment in a separate reconcile after the netting L6 gives 600 under both, because each pass starts with a fresh cache.

Under mutant A, all committed tests that reach this path pass: interest.db, ledger-oracle.db, chain.db, ledger.db, payment-terms.db, reconciliation-routes.db, chain.large.db and reconcile.large.db, 8 files and 165 of 165 tests.

The finding's citations hold:
- The existing one-line tests date rest-paid (2026-07-01) before netted (2026-08-03).
- The property at interest.test.ts:1118 always walks Z, Y, X, so X comes last, and it computes interestOutOfReach fresh rather than modelling the per-pass cache.
- The Stryker configs cover only ledger, money, packets and pricing, not apps/worker.

So a line this PR added that decides money has no test that fails without it. That is a real should-fix test gap. It is not a money error at head.

My scratch database (tp_i126d_skrvm32_1) has been dropped and the clone deleted. The probe test is kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/rvm32-interest-with-probe.db.test.ts.txt, and the verdict is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-sk-money-RVM3-2.md.

title: Two take-backs of one chain: the outcome depends on upload order (6.00 or 0.00, against 10.00 of cash). The worker's subtraction of the other take-backs, the only thing keeping the result at or below the cash, is pinned by no database test or property.
evidence: unplacedOf (remittances.ts:1123) passes every other take-back of the chain to interestUnplaced, which subtracts what each still owes (interest.ts:532-537). Mutant B2 passes [] instead. interest.db.test.ts and ledger-oracle.db.test.ts still pass, 56 of 56. Both order-independence properties also always pass takeBacks: [] (interest.test.ts:1167, :1249), so none generates a second take-back of one chain. A scratch model composes the pure functions as recordInterest does, with outOfReach the union over take-back L6s, unplaced over the other payments and take-backs, and walks in date order. Its shape: Y2 pays a 4.40 (dated first), Y1 pays a 1.00, X1 takes back a 3.00 and pays K1 6.00, X2 takes back a 4.40 and pays K2 6.00. All of a is on L1, weights unchanged throughout, cash 10.00. At the head, date order gives 6.00 (X1 is whole and K1 is written; X2 waits). Y2 uploaded last gives 0.00: X1's unplaced is 4.40 less X2's 4.40, X2's is 4.40 less X1's 2.00, and both wait for good. That contradicts ADR 0084 D5 (0084:142-148): 'the outcome is the one they give uploaded in order' while the weights are the same in either order. Without the subtraction (B2), Y2 uploaded last gives 12.00 against 10.00 of cash. Subtracting only the take-backs dated before the one being read gives 6.00 in both orders in the same model, and stays as safe: both can be whole only when the unplaced interest is at least what the two still owe together.
fix: Within 10.1's files. In unplacedOf, subtract only the other take-backs walked before this one, by bpr16_date, load and position, so unplaced interest completes take-backs in the order the reconcile walks them. Add an LED-24 database variant with two PLB L6s each netting a take-back of one chain against another patient's payment. It must fail under B2 and pin both orders. Extend the property at interest.test.ts:1118 to generate a second take-back and pass it as takeBacks. Or, if the order dependence stays, state it in D5 and the LED-24 row.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the finding. It holds on the current head, 98bb9c00, which has moved past 9824f4e9. unplacedOf is at remittances.ts:1116-1124 and the subtraction is at interest.ts:532-537. One part of it fails: the first fix it proposes is unsafe.

I reproduced it through the real worker in a database test. I wrote two synthetic fixtures copied from netted-elsewhere.835. zz-x1 reverses C's correction 240002 with AMT I -3.00, adds correction 240091, and pays the other patient 6.00 (PLB L6 -3.00). zz-x2 reverses 240091 with AMT I -4.40 and pays the other patient 6.00 (PLB L6 -1.60). The other two uploads are the existing partly-paid.835 (1.00) and rest-paid.835 (4.40). All reversals linked, and the draws came out as [K +600, C -300] and [K +600, C -440]. Cash is 10.00.
- At head: date order gives 6.00. With rest-paid.835 uploaded last it gives 0.00, because both take-backs wait for good.
- With mutant B2 (unplacedOf passes no take-backs): date order gives 6.00, and rest-paid.835 last gives 12.00, above the 10.00 of cash.
- Under B2, interest.db.test.ts and ledger-oracle.db.test.ts still pass in full: 54 tests from those two files, 56 counting my 2 scratch tests.
- Both properties pass takeBacks: [] (interest.test.ts:1167 and :1249) and model a single take-back. The unit tests at :739-746 pin the pure function but not the worker passing the take-backs in.

A pure model over all 24 upload orders agrees. Head gives 6.00 in 18 orders and 0.00 in the 6 with Y2 last, and never goes above cash. B2 gives 12.00 in 10 orders.

This contradicts what this PR claims. ADR 0084 D5 says "the outcome is the one they give uploaded in order" while the weights are unchanged. The "for good" exception covers only a take-back larger than what the uploads pay the chain, and X1's 3.00 is less than the 5.40 paid. The LED-24 row says the outcome is the same whichever is uploaded first. Both outcomes err low, so should-fix is the right severity. The money risk is that the one line keeping a netting payment within the cash is pinned by no database test or property.

The first fix it proposes is unsafe. "Subtract only the take-backs walked before this one" also gives 12.00 against 10.00 of cash in the pure model:
- Finding's shape, upload order Y1, X2, Y2, X1: X2 is completed by Y2's 4.40 and writes its 6.00. X1, dated earlier but uploaded later, is walked first, subtracts nothing, and writes its 6.00 too.
- Variant with X0 (4.40 back, dated before X1), upload order Y1, X1, Y2, X0: the same thing happens.

A take-back's payments are permanent once written, so the walk order is not the order in which take-backs were judged whole.

Use the finding's alternative instead:
- keep subtracting every other take-back;
- add an LED-24 database test with two netting PLB L6s of one chain that fails under B2;
- extend the property with a second take-back, asserting the result stays at or below the cash rather than that the orders match;
- state the order dependence in D5 and the LED-24 row.

The scratch clone is removed and database tp_i126d_skrvm33_1 is dropped. The fixtures, the database test and the model are saved as .txt files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/rvm33/. title: The out-of-reach cache invalidation in recordInterest is pinned by no test, though removing it credits the netted chain's interest to the wrong lines and loses another patient's 6.00
evidence:
The line in question is remittances.ts:1236, `interest.outOfReach.delete(adjustment.id);`. outOfReach[T] is cached before the take-back L6 T writes, because unplacedOf(T) calls paidLinesOf, which calls outOfReachOf over takeBacksOf(chain) and so includes T itself.

Mutant (the line replaced by a comment), at 98bb9c00: interest.db.test.ts, ledger-oracle.db.test.ts and ledger.db.test.ts pass 3/3 files and 99/99 tests. apps/worker is in no Stryker shard.

Scratch db scenario (synthetic twin, removed afterwards):
- The twin is zz-late-rest-paid.835: LED-24 one-line-rest-paid.835 with BPR16 2026-09-01, TRN02 SYNEFTLED24924 and ISA13/GS06 changed.
- Steps: case on original.835; load one-line-paid.835 and reconcile; load one-line-netted.835 (08-03) and the twin (09-01), then reconcile three times.

Results:
- Head: L1 [100, -100], L2 [600]. Interest 600 against 600 cash.
- Mutant: L1 [100, -100, 440], L2 []. Interest 440 against 600 cash.
- So with the mutant, the late payment of C1 lands on L1 after T reached it, T can never take it back and waits for good, and B's 6.00 is never written.

Why existing tests miss it: every committed variant either reconciles between uploads (fresh InterestState) or dates the payment before the netting L6. That covers interest.db.test.ts:598-627 and :676-694, 'with the second, before one reconcile' included: rest-paid 07-01 against netted 08-03.
fix: Add a db test with a payment of the chain dated after the netting L6, loaded with it before one reconcile (the one-line-netted.835 plus later-dated one-line-rest-paid twin above, expecting L1 [100, -100] and L2 [600], 600 against 600). Generate the twin through packages/synth and the LED-24 registry, not by hand.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute RV-DB3-2. I reproduced it at the branch head, 98bb9c00, in my own clone, which I have since removed.

1. The line is this PR's own. `interest.outOfReach.delete(adjustment.id)` at apps/worker/src/reconcile/remittances.ts:1236 came in with 1fda5637 (MONEY-R4-1). That commit is not an ancestor of origin/claude/build-platform, and the base's remittances.ts has no outOfReach at all.

2. The mechanism is as the finding says. For a take-back draw with mayYetHold, `unplacedOf` calls `paidLinesOf` and then `outOfReachOf`. That walks `takeBacksOf(chain)`, the L6 T itself included, and caches `interestOutOfReach` for T while T has written nothing. `reached = []`, so no line is out of reach. Once T writes −100 on L1, only the delete makes a later payment in the same pass see L1 as out of reach. The walk goes by payment date (providerAdjustments, D13), so a payment of the chain dated after T comes after T in the same pass.

3. Reproduction. The scratch twin was one-line-rest-paid.835 with ISA09/ISA13/GS04/GS06/GE/IEA, BPR16 20260901, TRN02 SYNEFTLED24924 and DTM405 changed. I appended a scratch test that was never committed. Steps: case on original.835, then one-line-paid.835 and a reconcile, then one-line-netted.835 and the twin, then reconciles.
   - Head: L1 [100, −100], L2 [600], interest 600 against 600 cash. This holds for both upload orders in one reconcile and for the twin in a later reconcile, and it agrees with the committed 'between them' result.
   - Mutant (the line commented out), both one-reconcile orders: L1 [100, −100, 440], L2 [], interest 440 against 600 cash. C1's 4.40 lands on L1, where T can no longer take it back, and B's 6.00 is never written. With the twin in a later reconcile it passes, as the finding predicts.

4. "Pinned by no test" holds. With the mutant applied I ran every db file that exercises PLB L6 interest. All passed:
   - interest.db.test.ts, ledger-oracle.db.test.ts, ledger.db.test.ts, reconciliation-routes.db.test.ts, payment-terms.db.test.ts and packages/db ledger-interest.db.test.ts: 6 files, 153 tests.
   - reconcile.large.db.test.ts and chain.large.db.test.ts: 2 tests.
   - The e2e spec, ledger-interest.spec.ts, covers only LED-23 payments with no take-back, so it cannot reach the line.
   - stryker/shards.json does not mention apps/worker.
   - The LED-24 registry variants in packages/synth workflow.ts are all one file per reconcile. The one committed one-reconcile case, rest-paid dated 07-01 with netted 08-03, dates the payment before the netting L6.

So the PR's own load-bearing cache invalidation has a reproducible, money-affecting failure when removed, and no test catches it. The finding stands as a should-fix test gap. Its proposed test (twin generated through packages/synth and the LED-24 registry; expect L1 [100, −100], L2 [600], 600/600) catches the mutant.
